name: Fintech Dashboard
pattern: Fixed left sidebar, top bar with search and account, then a KPI card row above a main chart and a dense transactions table.

rules.when: showing money or counts in a table
rules.do: right-align numbers, use tabular figures and a fixed number of decimals
show the delta with a sign and an arrow, never colour alone

rules.when: the page has more than four KPIs
rules.do: group them in one row of equal cards and push the rest into a detail view

rules.when: a destructive or irreversible money action
rules.do: ask for explicit confirmation naming the amount

avoid: decorative gradients behind data
pie charts with more than five slices
red and green as the only signal of gain and loss
dense tables without row hover and a sticky header
notes: Seed record written for OpenPencil. Trust comes from restraint: one accent colour, generous number typography, no ornament.

name: SaaS Landing Page
pattern: Hero with one headline and one primary call to action, social proof strip, three feature blocks, pricing, FAQ, closing call to action.

rules.do: state the outcome for the visitor in one line and repeat the same action label in the closing section
use three to six blocks with an icon, a short title and one sentence each
highlight one recommended plan and keep the plan comparison to the same rows
keep a slim sticky header with the primary action visible

avoid: more than one primary call to action per section
stock photo collages as the hero
walls of text in feature blocks
low-contrast grey body text on white
notes: Seed record written for OpenPencil. One accent colour carries every action so the eye always knows where to go next.

name: Mobile Health Tracker
pattern: Bottom tab bar with Today, Activity and Profile; Today shows a progress ring summary, then a vertical list of metric cards.

rules.do: lead with one large ring or number and the goal beside it

rules.when: a tap target sits on a phone
rules.do: make it at least 44 px tall with 8 px spacing to its neighbours
use neutral, supportive wording and no red alarm styling
offer steppers, pickers or quick chips before a keyboard

avoid: more than five bottom tabs
dense charts on the first screen
guilt-driven copy or streak-loss warnings
tiny grey labels under 12 px
notes: Seed record written for OpenPencil. Health data is personal: keep the first screen quiet and let one number lead.

name: E-commerce Storefront
pattern: Header with search and cart, category navigation, product grid with filters, product detail with gallery and sticky add-to-cart, short checkout.

rules.do: show image, name, price and one rating line, with the price as the strongest text
keep one prominent add-to-cart button that stays visible while scrolling the detail page
remove the main navigation and show a step indicator and the order total

rules.when: an item is out of stock
rules.do: say so on the card and offer to notify instead of hiding it

avoid: hidden shipping costs until the last step
auto-playing carousels as the main navigation
product images with inconsistent aspect ratios
forcing account creation before checkout
notes: Seed record written for OpenPencil. Photography does the selling: keep chrome neutral and let product images set the colour.

name: Developer Documentation
pattern: Three columns: section navigation on the left, readable article in the centre, on-this-page outline on the right, with a search box in the header.

rules.do: use a monospace face such as JetBrains Mono on a muted surface with a copy button
limit the line length to 65 to 80 characters
show method, path, parameters and a request and response example in the same order every time
keep search and the current section highlighted in the navigation

avoid: marketing hero sections inside the docs
light grey code text on white
navigation deeper than three levels
screenshots of code instead of text
notes: Seed record written for OpenPencil. The reader came to finish a task: speed of finding beats decoration.

name: Creative Portfolio
pattern: Minimal header, a large statement or hero work, a project grid of big images with titles on hover, then an about block and contact.

rules.do: give each project one large image and a one-line description; hide the rest behind a case study
keep the interface monochrome and let the work supply the colour, with one accent for links

rules.when: the grid has mixed image sizes
rules.do: align to a column grid and keep gutters equal
repeat a single contact action in the header and at the end

avoid: animated effects that delay seeing the work
more than two typefaces
thumbnails cropped so that the work is unreadable
contact forms with many required fields
notes: Seed record written for OpenPencil. The portfolio is a frame for the work; the design should step aside.
